claims.claim: By the best cell counts we have, a typical man is about half human.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML) + Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender: 'We estimate the total number of bacteria in the 70 kg "reference man" to be 3.8·10^13 ... revise past estimates to 3.0·10^13 human cells'; 30/68 = 44% human; B/H = 1.3 'with an uncertainty of 25%' gives roughly 38-51%. Hatton: '≈36 trillion cells in the male' (70 kg); with Sender's bacteria 36/74 = 49%. 'About half' is within A3 rounding. 'Typical man' = the 70 kg reference man (Sender's author summary: 'the typical adult human body consists of about 30 trillion human cells and about 38 trillion bacteria'). 'By the best cell counts' qualifies it as a count, not mass. 'Best' is an evaluative framing: these are the two most recent whole-body counts, and Hatton describes the earlier studies as 'converging on values of 30 to 37 trillion human cells'.

claims.claim: Hook at second two: a viewer who swipes away has heard 'By the best cell counts we have, a' and seen (Look 1) the dot figure with no label, (Look 2) 'BY CELL COUNT' over the Vitruvian Man.
claims.source_checked: alignment json (word 'typical' starts 2.176 s, 'half' 3.367 s); src/shorts/cell-count/index.tsx and cell-count-cutout/index.tsx (labels hang off 'about'/'half')
claims.note: No claim has been made by 2.0 s: the 'ABOUT HALF HUMAN' card and the 44% split start at 'about' (3.05 s) / 'half' (3.37 s), and both arrive with 'typical 70 kg man' / 'TYPICAL 70 KG MAN'. The popular false form (10:1 bacteria) is never stated or implied. A viewer leaving at 4 s gets the sourced claim with its qualifier.

claims.claim: About thirty trillion of your cells are yours.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML) + Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender: 3.0·10^13 human cells 'in the 70 kg "reference man"'; Hatton: '≈36 trillion cells in the male, ≈28 trillion in the female'. For the reference man 'about thirty' is fine (30 Sender, 36 Hatton). But 'your' addresses every viewer, and for a woman the sources disagree: Sender Table 3 'ref. woman ... 21' trillion, Hatton 28. A3: where sources disagree, make the narrower claim. Root cause shared by claims 3, 4, 9 and 16: after the hook, the voice switches to 'your', so the reference man's figures are told to every viewer. Sender's own Table 3 gives the reference woman 21 trillion human cells and 44 trillion bacteria (B:H 2.2), and other groups B:H 1.3-2.3 ('the B/H ratio varies by up to 2-fold across those different population groups'). The SOURCES block itself says the answer 'depends on' the body, which is why the hook names the man; the second-person lines drop that qualifier in the audio. CHANGE: keep the man as the subject, e.g. 'About thirty trillion of his cells are his own.' (or 'In that man, about thirty trillion cells are his own.').

claims.claim: Thirty-eight trillion are bacteria.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender: '3.8·10^13 bacteria in the colon with a standard error uncertainty of 25% and a variation of 52% SD over a population of 70 kg males', used as the whole-body figure for the 'reference man'; the authors' own summary says 'about 38 trillion bacteria'. Two problems: (a) said of 'your' cells, it contradicts Sender's reference woman (Table 3: 44 trillion bacteria); (b) the bare 'Thirty-eight trillion' is more precise than the source, which says 'about 38 trillion' with 25% uncertainty. CHANGE: 'About thirty-eight trillion are bacteria.' with the subject kept as the man (follows from the change to claim 3).

claims.claim: But put them all on a scale, and those bacteria weigh about two hundred grams.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender: 'we conclude that there is about 0.2 kg of bacteria in the body overall'; abstract: 'their total mass is about 0.2 kg'. Also 'about 0.3% of the body weight', 'significantly updating previous statements that 1%–3% of the body mass is composed of bacteria or that a normal human hosts 1–3 kg of bacteria [25]'. 'Those bacteria' refers back to the counted 38 trillion, so it is the reference man's figure; on screen the scale reads 'in a typical 70 kg man'.

claims.claim: And your own cells are not what you picture.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Framing line, no figure. It sets up the next claim (most human cells are enucleated red blood cells, not the textbook nucleated cell). Sender: 'almost 90% of the cells are estimated to be enucleated cells (26·10^12 cells), mostly red blood cells and platelets'. Holds for any viewer.

claims.claim: Most of them are red blood cells.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML) + Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender: 'The cell count is dominated by red blood cells (84%)'; '2.5·10^13 red blood cells (SEM 2%, CV 12%)' of 3.0·10^13. Sender applies the same 84% to every group in Table 3 (footnote 2), so 'most' holds for any viewer. Hatton: 'Cell counts are completely dominated by red blood cells, platelets, and tissue resident white blood cells'; 'nonnucleated blood cells (≈29 trillion)' of ≈36 trillion (red cells and platelets together; Hatton's main text gives no separate red-cell count, so the spoken 'most' rests on Sender's 84%).

claims.claim: By count, your cells are mostly blood.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML) + Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender: 'the dominant role of the hematopoietic lineage to the total count (≈90%)'; 'the body includes only 3·10^12 non-blood human cells, merely 10% of the total'. Hatton agrees (counts dominated by red cells, platelets and white blood cells). 'By count' is said, and correctly so: by mass Sender says '75% of total cell mass is composed of two cell types, fat cells (adipocytes) and muscle cells (myocytes)'.

claims.claim: And their passengers roughly match them, cell for cell.
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: For the reference man, Sender: 'B/H = 1.3, with an uncertainty of 25% ... This B/H value of about 1:1 ... should replace the 10:1 or 100:1 values', so 'roughly match' is fine for him. But 'their' = 'your cells' (previous line), i.e. every viewer, and Sender's Table 3 gives 'ref. woman ... 21 [human] 44 [bacteria] 2.2', 'young infant ... 2.3', 'elder ... 1.8'. A 2.2:1 ratio is not 'roughly match, cell for cell'. The on-screen 'typical 70 kg man' scrap does not reach audio-only listeners, and the SOURCES entry itself says this holds 'for the typical man of the hook'. Root cause shared by claims 3, 4, 9 and 16: after the hook, the voice switches to 'your', so the reference man's figures are told to every viewer. Sender's own Table 3 gives the reference woman 21 trillion human cells and 44 trillion bacteria (B:H 2.2), and other groups B:H 1.3-2.3 ('the B/H ratio varies by up to 2-fold across those different population groups'). The SOURCES block itself says the answer 'depends on' the body, which is why the hook names the man; the second-person lines drop that qualifier in the audio. CHANGE: put the man back in the closing line, e.g. 'And in a typical man, the passengers roughly match them, cell for cell.' (or 'And his passengers roughly match them, cell for cell.' if claims 3-4 move to 'his').

claims.note: 'Bacteria overwhelmingly outnumber eukaryotes and archaea in the human microbiome by 2–3 orders of magnitude. We therefore sometimes operationally refer to the microbial cells in the human body as bacteria.'

claims.claim: Hatton's 36 trillion is within 'about thirty' at A3's limit; on screen the 30 trillion is marked as the 2016 count in both looks
claims.source_checked: Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: 36 → 'about thirty' is a 17% rounding, inside A3's stated outer limit (1.7e5 → 'about a hundred thousand'). Both looks tag the first '30 TRILLION' with 2016 ('(2016 count)', '· 2016 COUNT', '(2016)'). Look 1's last card '30 TRILLION / yours, mostly blood' has no year; that is acceptable once the figure has been tagged.

claims.claim: 3.8e13 nearly all in the colon; colon estimate 'in some respects ... an upper limit'
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: 'The vast majority of the bacteria reside in the colon'; other organs 'at most 10^12'; 'In some respects, the estimate we performed ... can be considered an upper limit.'

claims.claim: Earlier statements of 1-3 kg (1-3% of body mass), citing a 2012 NIH news release
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: 'previous statements that 1%–3% of the body mass is composed of bacteria or that a normal human hosts 1–3 kg of bacteria [25]'; ref 25 = NIH, 'NIH Human Microbiome Project defines normal bacterial makeup of the body', 2012 news release.

claims.claim: Sender: 'The cell count is dominated by red blood cells (84%)', 2.5e13 of 3.0e13; Hatton: non-nucleated blood cells (red cells and platelets) ≈29 of ≈36 trillion
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML) + Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Sender quoted exactly. Hatton: 'Even after removing nonnucleated blood cells (≈29 trillion) ...' and 'dominated by red blood cells and platelets'. The SOURCES block paraphrases this accurately.

claims.claim: '75% of total cell mass is composed of two cell types, fat cells (adipocytes) and muscle cells (myocytes)'; red blood cells 'among the smallest cell types in the human body'
claims.source_checked: Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLoS Biol 14(8):e1002533, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533; full text PMC4991899 (Europe PMC fullTextXML) + Hatton et al. 2023, PNAS 120(39):e2303077120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2303077120; full text PMC10523466 (Europe PMC fullTextXML)
claims.note: Both quotes are exact (Sender). Hatton: 'cell biomass is dominated by muscle and fat (myocytes and adipocytes)'.
